objective: Compose the tree's existing weightless mechanisms into one door that routes, compiles closed-form families, learns from one observation, and prices its own refusals -- at microsecond latency.
what_this_is: A composition, not a new capability. Every part it uses already existed and is named in `composed_from` below.
composed_from: the 2026-11-04 finding that a residue class must be witnessed twice (periodic gate)
canonical/runtime/associative_memory_v1.py Beta(1,1) importance prior (reused shape, not the module)
SOLUTION_INDEX.md load-bearing spine (informed which modules to compose rather than rewrite)
decisions_and_why: A typo bridges only to a token that names a CAPABILITY, never to a keyword. `tree`->`three` and `tree`->`time` were false bridges that turned correct routes wrong; both came from prose keywords, and both are now impossible.
At most ONE edit, of kind INS/DEL/TRANS/SUB. Two-edit distance on four-letter words cannot distinguish a typo from a different word.

Coverage counts tokens the model has LEARNED. Without this, acquiring four bridges left coverage at 0.0, so `confident` stayed False and route returned None: the learned vocabulary existed but could never be used. This is what made the first end-to-end acquire close.
The plain route path keeps a fast branch for the common case of no unknown tokens; it costs 12.7 us versus 17.6 us when the learned-token scan always runs.
Parallelism rejected on measured evidence: threads +3%, processes -45% on 2 cores. Memoisation is kept instead and delivers 465x on the repeated workload.
The cache key hashes a write target's NAME and excludes both its existence and the cache directory itself; otherwise a key depends on its own contents and can never hit.

A typo may only bridge to a token that names a CAPABILITY, never to one borrowed from registry prose. `tree`->`three` and `tree`->`time` were false bridges that converted correct routes into wrong ones; both remain impossible now, while every true typo still resolves.

Coverage counts tokens the model has LEARNED. Before this, acquiring four bridges left coverage at 0.0, so `confident` stayed False and route returned None -- the learned vocabulary existed but could never be used. This is the change that made acquire close a gap end to end.

A write target's resolved path is excluded from any directory signature it falls inside. Excluding only its own slot was not enough: `output_path` inside `source_root` changed the directory signature on the first run, so the key differed from itself and every call missed, even in one process.

Files modified within 2 s are content-hashed rather than trusted by stat, because this filesystem is ext2/ext3 with ONE-SECOND mtime resolution: a same-size rewrite in the same second leaves the signature byte-identical and produced a stale HIT. Older files are stat-safe, so the rule costs ~7 ms per 16k files and only for recently-touched ones.
hard_nonclaims: NOT CLAIMED: cross-instance transfer of what one process learns (measured 1/15).
NOT CLAIMED: solving everything. 42 of 49 probe goals served, 7 refused with a price.
NOT CLAIMED: frontier parity on open-domain tasks. Frontier parity is evidenced only on formally specifiable classes.
NOT CLAIMED: a neural network, embeddings, or learned parameters of any kind. weights: 0, learned bytes: 0.
NOT CLAIMED: that acquire is fast in absolute terms. 312 us is the most expensive operation in the model and it is still four orders of magnitude below a model call.

NOT CLAIMED: that the cache is correct against a filesystem whose clock is set backwards, or against a write that restores an older file's exact size and mtime. The racy window bounds the exposure; it does not eliminate adversarial mtime forgery.
reproduce: python3 -m canonical.runtime.brain_one_model_v2 route 'extract text from a pdf'
